That's the one that we received. And then D104/1. And I would also be asking perhaps that we mark for identification and at least tender at this point so it's on the record the three documents that were given by the Prosecution this afternoon, the interview between Wajid Zia, Costello, and Miroslav Deronjic, 4 May. And perhaps we could give it to you, 108/1, with A, B, and C, A being the document entitled interview; B being the declaration of investigator, Mr. Zia; and C being the typewritten, abbreviated notes of Mr. Costello, dated 4/5/02.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, D96/1, as Mr. Karnavas has stated, the understanding of the parties, should normally be something you have as part of the plea agreement. It was read into one of his statements that is evidence. But it should come in in this form as well, so we have no objection to that. The other matters, the previous statements, I think it's a good rule, but to the degree the Court feels these would be helpful in their analysis, I would not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Karnavas, as you rightly pointed out, generally speaking, we do not admit the previous statement of the witness into the evidence. Since we have the witness here and you have conducted considerable cross-examination to this witness. But since we have already admitted the statement, the latest statement of this witness, and we believe that the previous statements are somehow related to this statement. So under these circumstances in order for the Trial Chamber to have an overall assessment of the truthfulness of this witness and to see the testimony of the witness and an overall picture, as an exception we admit all those documents you ask into the evidence. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just so the Court is clear, as you know Mr. Deronjic has given so many statements. His final statement that you admitted through 92 bis is a synopsis of a series of -- it must be eight or nine days of tapes. And I don't think that was part of what Mr. Karnavas offered. But -- and we have not offered it, because it's mostly to do with 1992. But I -- just to be clear, that would be the whole Deronjic package, if that's the intention, not to overburden you with material. But that is the -- you will see that in the synopsis there are references in the synopsis and particular facts where Mr. Deronjic speaks more -- in more detail. And so if you, for example, get to the part about -- there will be a very brief statement about the six strategic objectives and then it will cite to the tape statement where he will talk about it for three or four pages. So I don't know if you want all of it, but that's all there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you mean document D108/1, A, B, and C?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You mean of this -- the recent notes we have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, that's different. The there were -- there's volumes of interviews after Mr. Deronjic's arrest pursuant to the plea agreements where he talked at length about -- mostly about 1992. And what we have provided is a synopsis of that. There are two tapes from that series of interviews where Srebrenica was specifically dealt with. And I'm not sure if Mr. Karnavas tabbed those for evidence or we did, but I think Mr. Karnavas did. So part of those tapes are in, but there's a whole series of others that are not, but are referred to in the synopsis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think Mr. Karnavas offered some documents which is in the written form with the D numbers as he read out just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And as you'll see, two of those documents I believe are part of this larger interview. And just so you know now, if you review those, you will see that there are many other tapes. So I just want to let you know, if you want the whole thing, we have that. Everybody has been provided it in discovery, but it's a lot, that's why we've kept to the synopsis, because it's mostly 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We only entertain whatever the Defence counsel tendered, which is limited to the numbers he read out just now. I don't think that will include any tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's fine. I think we do have transcripts of that material, but again I didn't think it was necessary for this proceeding, and it's just a lot of extra work and reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since there's no -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand what Mr. McCloskey is referring to. I had, unfortunately, the task of reading all of that several times, all the volumes. There are some tapes that are strictly related to Glogova. They are interesting but not necessarily relevant to this case. And that's why we didn't tender them. I don't object to all of them coming in, somebody -- but if they're going to come in, they should be read. I don't know if that's necessary. But if they want to get the full flavour, that's fine. But we're talking hundreds and hundreds of pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, we'll only admit those written documents in the written form. So I see there's no objections from Mr. McCloskey, so the document tendered by the Defence team is admitted into the evidence. Well, Mr. Deronjic, thank you very much indeed for your willingness to testify. And today is the first day of the Chinese New Year. I will take this opportunity to wish you good luck in the new year, the year of monkey. And we wish you good luck, especially in your sentencing hearing which is scheduled next week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. And I would like to wish you a Happy New Year as well, and I wish everybody all the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The usher will take you out of the room. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting. There is a technical matter I'm told by Mr. Registrar here. 108 should actually be 108.1, .2, and .3, and not A, B, C. I hesitate to mention it, but I'm getting these looks. So I assume that we want a clear record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey, are there any changes in the witness list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, nothing seems to be easy, but I have -- we just in the last day or two communicated with Mr. Stojanovic regarding the upcoming handwriting expert. And this is an issue that I had spoken with Ms. Sinatra about before when we first got the books. And just to confirm that we did not have access to Mr. Jokic's handwriting samples. I recently sent a letter to Mr. Stojanovic to that effect. And he tells me that he and Mr. Jokic have now agreed to provide a handwriting sample. Now, it has to do mostly, I believe, with the material in the workbook provided by Mr. Obrenovic, which as you're aware has some rather significant entries in it. So it is a significant issue. And I think in that -- this science of handwriting expertise is part of our evidence, we have -- are now in the process of speaking to the expert to see if this offer of a new handwriting -- or a handwriting example or examples would assist her in her viewpoint. I haven't heard back from her yet. My guess is the answer would be yes, which I am trying to push to be able to get the examples, get them to her, get her test, and then get her here -- get her report and get her here, of course, by the end of the trial -- our case, which February 6th stands out as a date I don't want to fool around with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you think that we could finish the testimony of the next witness in one day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I have spoken to Mr. Karnavas, and as a day or two ago, we think we should be able to finish this next witness tomorrow. It should be a short witness and it really has nothing to do with Mr. Stojanovic's situation. So we should be ready -- we shouldn't have a problem. And I've just gotten a note. We have spoken to Ms. Barr and she will be able to do her analysis in one day, and so hopefully we will -- and she will be available Thursday or Friday next week. So it looks like we're on track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But first of all, I think we need that latest report concerning of the new signatures before her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course. I've spoken to Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Jokic is available tomorrow afternoon. And we will get the FedEx to -- the person is in the United Kingdom and it will take one day. So we will make sure everybody has this hopefully one or two days beforehand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that's all for today. We have been sitting for a long time, and we'll resume at 9.00 in Courtroom III. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 4.40 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of January, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
